qa_pairs.explanation: The proportion of those having a physical examination once a year is 35.48% × the proportion of those concerned about the 'Tumor Markers' indicator is 30.67% = 0.3548 × 0.3067 = 0.10881716. Rounding to 2 decimal places gives 10.88%.

qa_pairs.question: Based on the chart of consumers' physical examination frequencies and the chart of the most concerned health indicators, what possible differences might there be in the concerns about health indicators between consumers who have regular physical examinations (such as once a year or once every two years) and those who have fewer physical examinations (such as not having a check - up without illness or never having had a physical examination)? Which options can best explain these differences?

answer.A: Since the proportion of those having a physical examination once a year is the highest (35.48%), consumers with regular physical examinations are most concerned about the Helicobacter pylori indicator (35.57%), which reflects their emphasis on digestive system health.
answer.B: Consumers who have fewer physical examinations (not having a check - up without illness or never having had a physical examination, with a total proportion of 21.01%) are more concerned about functional examinations (such as radiology and ultrasound), because the proportion of this type of indicator is the highest (46.28%) and it is related to emergency diagnostic needs.
answer.C: The overall distribution of consumers' physical examination frequencies (mainly regular physical examinations) may explain why the proportion of concern for basic indicators such as biochemical tests is the highest, while the proportion of concern for specific indicators such as HPV is relatively low, reflecting the general trend of preventive health management.
answer.D: Consumers with regular physical examinations are more concerned about specific disease indicators (such as HPV or tumor markers) because they hope to prevent serious diseases through targeted examinations; while consumers with fewer physical examinations are more concerned about basic indicators (such as clinical examination items) because they only conduct simple evaluations when symptoms appear.
answer.E: Consumers with regular physical examinations are more inclined to focus on basic health indicators (such as clinical examination items and biochemical tests) because they maintain healthy habits through regular examinations, while consumers with fewer physical examinations may be more concerned about specific disease indicators (such as HPV or tumor markers) because they only seek examinations when health concerns arise.
answer.F: The group with a higher frequency of physical examinations has relatively lower concern for functional examination indicators (such as radiology or electrocardiogram) because these indicators are usually related to in - depth diagnosis, while regular physical examinations focus more on preventive basic indicators; the group with fewer physical examinations may be more concerned about these functional indicators due to sudden needs.
